2.mohsin_khan: By the ten nights (i.e. the first ten days of the month of Dhul-Hijjah).

3.sahih_international: And [by] the even [number] and the odd
3.pickthall: And the Even and the Odd,
3.shakir: And the even and the odd,
3.muhammad_sarwar: by the odd and even (8th and 9th Dhil-hajj)
3.mohsin_khan: And by the even and the odd (of all the creations of Allah).
3.arberry: by the even and the odd,

4.sahih_international: And [by] the night when it passes,
4.pickthall: And the night when it departeth,
4.yusuf_ali: And by the Night when it passeth away;-
4.shakir: And the night when it departs.
4.muhammad_sarwar: and by the night when it moves on towards daybreak (reward and retribution in the next life is an absolute reality).
4.mohsin_khan: And by the night when it departs.
4.arberry: by the night when it journeys on!

5.sahih_international: Is there [not] in [all] that an oath [sufficient] for one of perception?
5.pickthall: There surely is an oath for thinking man.
5.yusuf_ali: Is there (not) in these an adjuration (or evidence) for those who understand?
5.shakir: Truly in that there is an oath for those who possess understanding.
5.muhammad_sarwar: Is this not a sufficient oath for intelligent people?
5.mohsin_khan: There is indeed in them (the above oaths) sufficient proofs for men of understanding (and that, they should avoid all kinds of sins and disbeliefs, etc.)!
5.arberry: Is there in that an oath for a mindful man?

6.sahih_international: Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with 'Aad -
6.pickthall: Dost thou not consider how thy Lord dealt with (the tribe of) A'ad,
6.yusuf_ali: Seest thou not how thy Lord dealt with the 'Ad (people),-
6.shakir: Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with Ad,
6.muhammad_sarwar: (Muhammad), consider how your Lord dealt with the tribe of Ad,
6.mohsin_khan: Did you (O Muhammad (Peace be upon him)) not see (thought) how your Lord dealt with 'Ad (people)?
6.arberry: Hast thou not seen how thy Lord did with Ad,

7.yusuf_ali: Of the (city of) Iram, with lofty pillars,
7.shakir: (The people of) Aram, possessors of lofty buildings,
7.muhammad_sarwar: the people of the huge columned city of Eram
7.mohsin_khan: Who were very tall like lofty pillars,

8.sahih_international: The likes of whom had never been created in the land?
8.pickthall: The like of which was not created in the lands;
8.yusuf_ali: The like of which were not produced in (all) the land?
8.shakir: The like of which were not created in the (other) cities;
8.muhammad_sarwar: whose like has never been created in any other land.
8.mohsin_khan: The like of which were not created in the land?
8.arberry: the like of which was never created in the land,

9.sahih_international: And [with] Thamud, who carved out the rocks in the valley?
9.pickthall: And with (the tribe of) Thamud, who clove the rocks in the valley;
9.yusuf_ali: And with the Thamud (people), who cut out (huge) rocks in the valley?-
9.shakir: And (with) Samood, who hewed out the rocks in the valley,
9.muhammad_sarwar: (Also consider how He dealt with) the Thamud, who carved their houses out of the rocks in the valley.
9.mohsin_khan: And (with) Thamud (people), who cut (hewed) out rocks in the valley (to make dwellings)?
9.arberry: and Thamood, who hollowed the rocks in the valley,

10.sahih_international: And [with] Pharaoh, owner of the stakes? -
10.pickthall: And with Pharaoh, firm of might,
10.yusuf_ali: And with Pharaoh, lord of stakes?
10.shakir: And (with) Firon, the lord of hosts,
10.muhammad_sarwar: (Also consider the people of) the Pharaoh who victimized people by placing them on the stake,
10.mohsin_khan: And (with) Fir'aun (Pharaoh), who had pegs (who used to torture men by binding them to pegs)?
10.arberry: and Pharaoh, he of the tent-pegs,

11.sahih_international: [All of] whom oppressed within the lands
11.pickthall: Who (all) were rebellious (to Allah) in these lands,
11.yusuf_ali: (All) these transgressed beyond bounds in the lands,
11.shakir: Who committed inordinacy in the cities,
11.mohsin_khan: Who did transgress beyond bounds in the lands (in the disobedience of Allah).
11.arberry: who all were insolent in the land

12.shakir: So they made great mischief therein?
12.muhammad_sarwar: and spread much corruption in the land.

13.sahih_international: So your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment.
13.pickthall: Therefore thy Lord poured on them the disaster of His punishment.
13.yusuf_ali: Therefore did thy Lord pour on them a scourge of diverse chastisements:
13.shakir: Therefore your Lord let down upon them a portion of the chastisement.
13.muhammad_sarwar: Thus, your Lord afflicted them with torment;
13.mohsin_khan: So your Lord poured on them different kinds of severe torment.
13.arberry: Thy Lord unloosed on them a scourge of chastisement;

14.sahih_international: Indeed, your Lord is in observation.
14.pickthall: Lo! thy Lord is ever watchful.
14.yusuf_ali: For thy Lord is (as a Guardian) on a watch-tower.
14.shakir: Most surely your Lord is watching.
14.muhammad_sarwar: your Lord keeps an eye on (all evil-doing people).
14.mohsin_khan: Verily, your Lord is Ever Watchful (over them).
14.arberry: surely thy Lord is ever on the watch.

15.sahih_international: And as for man, when his Lord tries him and [thus] is generous to him and favors him, he says, "My Lord has honored me."
15.pickthall: As for man, whenever his Lord trieth him by honouring him, and is gracious unto him, he saith: My Lord honoureth me.
15.yusuf_ali: Now, as for man, when his Lord trieth him, giving him honour and gifts, then saith he, (puffed up), "My Lord hath honoured me."
15.shakir: And as for man, when his Lord tries him, then treats him with honor and makes him lead an easy life, he says: My Lord honors me.
15.muhammad_sarwar: As for the human being, when his Lord tests him, honors him, and grants him bounty, he says, "God has honored me".
15.mohsin_khan: As for man, when his Lord tries him by giving him honour and gifts, then he says (puffed up): "My Lord has honoured me."
15.arberry: As for man, whenever his Lord tries him, and honours him, and blesses him, then he says, 'My Lord has honoured me.'

16.sahih_international: But when He tries him and restricts his provision, he says, "My Lord has humiliated me."
16.pickthall: But whenever He trieth him by straitening his means of life, he saith: My Lord despiseth me.
16.yusuf_ali: But when He trieth him, restricting his subsistence for him, then saith he (in despair), "My Lord hath humiliated me!"
16.shakir: But when He tries him (differently), then straitens to him his means of subsistence, he says: My Lord has disgraced me.
16.muhammad_sarwar: However, when his Lord tests him by a measured amount of sustenance, he says, "God has disgraced me".
16.mohsin_khan: But when He tries him, by straitening his means of life, he says: "My Lord has humiliated me!"
16.arberry: But when he tries him and stints for him his provision, then he says, 'My Lord has despised me.'

17.sahih_international: No! But you do not honor the orphan
17.pickthall: Nay, but ye (for your part) honour not the orphan
17.yusuf_ali: Nay, nay! but ye honour not the orphans!
17.shakir: Nay! but you do not honor the orphan,
17.muhammad_sarwar: (Since wealth does not necessarily guarantee everlasting happiness) then why do you not show kindness to the orphans,
17.mohsin_khan: Nay! But you treat not the orphans with kindness and generosity (i.e. you neither treat them well, nor give them their exact right of inheritance)!
17.arberry: No indeed; but you honour not the orphan,

18.sahih_international: And you do not encourage one another to feed the poor.
18.pickthall: And urge not on the feeding of the poor.
18.yusuf_ali: Nor do ye encourage one another to feed the poor!-
18.shakir: Nor do you urge one another to feed the poor,
18.muhammad_sarwar: or urge one another to feed the destitute?
18.mohsin_khan: And urge not on the feeding of AlMiskin (the poor)!
18.arberry: and you urge not the feeding of the needy,

19.sahih_international: And you consume inheritance, devouring [it] altogether,
19.pickthall: And ye devour heritages with devouring greed.
19.yusuf_ali: And ye devour inheritance - all with greed,
19.shakir: And you eat away the heritage, devouring (everything) indiscriminately,
19.muhammad_sarwar: Why do you take away the inheritance of others indiscriminately
19.mohsin_khan: And you devour inheritance all with greed,
19.arberry: and you devour the inheritance greedily,

20.sahih_international: And you love wealth with immense love.
20.pickthall: And love wealth with abounding love.
20.yusuf_ali: And ye love wealth with inordinate love!
20.shakir: And you love wealth with exceeding love.
20.muhammad_sarwar: and why do you have an excessive love of riches?
20.mohsin_khan: And you love wealth with much love!
20.arberry: and you love wealth with an ardent love

21.sahih_international: No! When the earth has been leveled - pounded and crushed -
21.pickthall: Nay, but when the earth is ground to atoms, grinding, grinding,
21.yusuf_ali: Nay! When the earth is pounded to powder,
21.shakir: Nay! when the earth is made to crumble to pieces,
21.muhammad_sarwar: When the earth is crushed into small pieces
21.mohsin_khan: Nay! When the earth is ground to powder,
21.arberry: No indeed! When the earth is ground to powder,

22.sahih_international: And your Lord has come and the angels, rank upon rank,
22.pickthall: And thy Lord shall come with angels, rank on rank,
22.yusuf_ali: And thy Lord cometh, and His angels, rank upon rank,
22.shakir: And your Lord comes and (also) the angels in ranks,
22.muhammad_sarwar: and (when you find yourself) in the presence of your Lord and the rows and rows of angels, your greed for riches will certainly be of no avail to you.
22.mohsin_khan: And your Lord comes with the angels in rows,
22.arberry: and thy Lord comes, and the angels rank on rank,

23.sahih_international: And brought [within view], that Day, is Hell - that Day, man will remember, but what good to him will be the remembrance?
23.pickthall: And hell is brought near that day; on that day man will remember, but how will the remembrance (then avail him)?
23.yusuf_ali: And Hell, that Day, is brought (face to face),- on that Day will man remember, but how will that remembrance profit him?
23.shakir: And hell is made to appear on that day. On that day shall man be mindful, and what shall being mindful (then) avail him?
23.muhammad_sarwar: On that day, hell will be brought closer and the human being will come to his senses, but this will be of no avail to him.
23.mohsin_khan: And Hell will be brought near that Day. On that Day will man remember, but how will that remembrance (then) avail him?
23.arberry: and Gehenna is brought out, upon that day man will remember; and how shall the Reminder be for him?

24.sahih_international: He will say, "Oh, I wish I had sent ahead [some good] for my life."
24.pickthall: He will say: Ah, would that I had sent before me (some provision) for my life!
24.yusuf_ali: He will say: "Ah! Would that I had sent forth (good deeds) for (this) my (Future) Life!"
24.shakir: He shall say: O! would that I had sent before for (this) my life!
24.muhammad_sarwar: He will say, "Would that I had done some good deeds for this life".
24.mohsin_khan: He will say: "Alas! Would that I had sent forth (good deeds) for (this) my life!"
24.arberry: He shall say, 'O would that I had forwarded for my life!'

25.sahih_international: So on that Day, none will punish [as severely] as His punishment,
25.pickthall: None punisheth as He will punish on that day!
25.yusuf_ali: For, that Day, His Chastisement will be such as none (else) can inflict,
25.shakir: But on that day shall no one chastise with (anything like) His chastisement,
25.muhammad_sarwar: On that day the punishment of God and His detention will be unparalleled.
25.mohsin_khan: So on that Day, none will punish as He will punish.
25.arberry: Upon that day none shall chastise as He chastises,

26.sahih_international: And none will bind [as severely] as His binding [of the evildoers].
26.pickthall: None bindeth as He then will bind.
26.yusuf_ali: And His bonds will be such as none (other) can bind.
26.shakir: And no one shall bind with (anything like) His binding.
26.muhammad_sarwar: And His bonds will be such as none other can bind.
26.mohsin_khan: And none will bind as He will bind.
26.arberry: none shall bind as He binds.

27.sahih_international: [To the righteous it will be said], "O reassured soul,
27.pickthall: But ah! thou soul at peace!
27.yusuf_ali: (To the righteous soul will be said:) "O (thou) soul, in (complete) rest and satisfaction!
27.shakir: O soul that art at rest!
27.mohsin_khan: (It will be said to the pious): "O (you) the one in (complete) rest and satisfaction!

28.sahih_international: Return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him],
28.pickthall: Return unto thy Lord, content in His good pleasure!
28.yusuf_ali: "Come back thou to thy Lord,- well pleased (thyself), and well-pleasing unto Him!
28.shakir: Return to your Lord, well-pleased (with him), well-pleasing (Him),
28.muhammad_sarwar: return to your Lord well pleased with him and He will be pleased with you.
28.mohsin_khan: "Come back to your Lord, Well-pleased (yourself) and well-pleasing unto Him!
28.arberry: return unto thy Lord, well-pleased, well-pleasing!

29.mohsin_khan: "Enter you, then, among My honoured slaves,
